digest.component_or_area: rebar._store git operations under high local concurrency
propositions: Concurrent rebar sessions contend on shared local git lock files (.git/index.lock, ref locks) and surface errors instead of absorbing transient contention, causing agent failures under normal high-concurrency operation.

Local-only git call sites in compact, delete, fsck, txn, event_append, and metrics modules lack both contention policy and per-site timeout bounds, creating unbounded stalls that can cascade into fleet-wide agent stalls while holding the store write lock.

A transient lock conflict held briefly by a peer process should resolve silently after bounded jittered retry rather than escalating to the caller; only a genuinely stuck lock (budget exhausted) should surface one actionable error naming the lock file and holder guidance.

Rebar must serialize its own writers via a per-store advisory lock and apply jittered exponential backoff (matching git's lockfile.c pattern) at the shared git execution seam so every routed call site inherits the contention policy without per-site changes.

Uncontended store git operations must add zero latency (non-blocking advisory lock on happy path), and watchdog timeouts on purely local git calls must be bounded at generous levels (120s for plumbing, 300s for slow walks like blame/log) to distinguish wedged filesystems from legitimately slow work.
